newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BUX hits 12th record in row at 4,463.47pts.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BUX hits 12th record in row at 4,463.47pts.

text.p: A wave of foreign interest in Hungarian stocks pushed the BUX share index of the Budapest Stock Exchange to its 12th record high in a row, dealers said.
The index of the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) rose 4.0 percent or 173.18 points to close at 4,463.47.
"The upgrade by Moody's of Hungary's credit rating in December seems to have tempted some large investment funds to pour money into Hungarian stocks," said Daiwa-MKB's Adam Santha.
Santha said the main beneficiaries of the spending spree were chemicals companies TVK and Borsodchem, oil company MOL, and hotel chain Danubius, all of which made strong gains.
TVK closed at 2,080, up 95, Borsodchem at 4375, up 170, MOL at 2,355 forints, up 155, and Danubius at 4380, up 80.
Retailer Fotex also rose to 130, up 14, and has gained 30 percent in two days.
"A specific investor seems to be concentrating on Fotex," Santha said.
Laszlo Baranyi of Gog Securities said it was inpossible to predict when the current bull run would end.
"It will stop when the investment funds run out of cash," he said, and predicted steady rises, punctuated by the odd correction for 1997, as he believed Hungarian shares were still cheap.
